questions.question: What is the SI unit of electric charge?
questions.explanation: The SI unit of electric charge is the Coulomb (C), named after Charles-Augustin de Coulomb.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of electric current?
questions.explanation: The SI unit of electric current is the Ampere (A), defined as 1 Coulomb of charge flowing per second (1 A = 1 C/s).

questions.question: What is the SI unit of electrical potential difference?
questions.explanation: Potential difference is measured in Volts (V), where 1 Volt = 1 Joule per Coulomb (1 V = 1 J/C).

questions.question: What is the SI unit of electrical resistance?
questions.explanation: Electrical resistance is measured in Ohms (Ω), named in honor of Georg Simon Ohm.

questions.question: What is the mathematical formulation of Ohm's Law?
questions.explanation: Ohm's law states that potential difference V across a conductor is directly proportional to current I at constant temperature: V = IR.

questions.question: What is the formula for electric power in terms of voltage (V) and current (I)?
questions.explanation: Electric power is the rate at which electrical energy is converted: P = VI (or P = I²R = V²/R).

questions.question: What is the SI unit of electrical capacitance?
questions.explanation: Capacitance is measured in Farads (F), named after Michael Faraday (1 F = 1 C/V).

questions.question: What is the commercial unit of electrical energy (1 Board of Trade unit)?
questions.explanation: The commercial unit of electric energy is the kilowatt-hour (kWh), where 1 kWh = 3.6 × 10⁶ J.

questions.question: What is the value of Coulomb's electrostatic constant k in vacuum?
questions.explanation: In vacuum, Coulomb's constant k = 1 / (4πε₀) ≈ 9 × 10⁹ N·m²/C².

questions.question: What instrument is used to detect the presence and nature of electric charge on a body?
questions.explanation: A gold-leaf electroscope is an electrostatic instrument used to detect electric charge and identify whether it is positive or negative.

questions.question: Who discovered that an electric current creates a magnetic field around itself?
questions.explanation: In 1820, Danish physicist Hans Christian Oersted discovered that a current-carrying wire deflects a nearby magnetic compass needle.

questions.question: Which rule gives the direction of the magnetic field around a straight current-carrying wire?
questions.explanation: According to the Right-Hand Grip Rule, if the right thumb points along current, the curled fingers indicate the direction of magnetic field lines.

questions.question: Which device converts electrical energy into mechanical energy?
questions.explanation: An electric motor utilizes magnetic forces on a current-carrying coil to convert electrical energy into mechanical rotation.

questions.question: Which device converts mechanical energy into electrical energy?
questions.explanation: An electric generator (or dynamo) rotates a coil inside a magnetic field to convert mechanical work into electrical energy.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of magnetic field strength (magnetic flux density)?
questions.explanation: The SI unit of magnetic flux density B is the Tesla (T), where 1 T = 1 N / (A·m) = 1 Wb/m².

questions.question: What component in a DC motor reverses the current in the coil every half rotation?
questions.explanation: The split-ring commutator acts as a mechanical switch that reverses current flow through the armature loop every 180° to sustain continuous unidirectional rotation.

questions.question: Which law states that the direction of an induced EMF always opposes the change in magnetic flux producing it?
questions.explanation: Lenz's Law states that the polarity of induced EMF creates an induced current whose magnetic field opposes the original flux change.

questions.question: What type of transformer increases alternating voltage from primary to secondary?
questions.explanation: A step-up transformer has more secondary turns than primary turns (Ns > Np), increasing output voltage (Vs > Vp).

questions.question: What type of transformer decreases alternating voltage from primary to secondary?
questions.explanation: A step-down transformer has fewer turns on the secondary than on the primary coil (Ns < Np), reducing secondary voltage.

questions.question: What is the formula for the turns and voltage ratio of an ideal transformer?
questions.explanation: For an ideal transformer, the voltage ratio equals the turns ratio: Vp / Vs = Np / Ns.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of electrical resistivity?
questions.explanation: From R = ρL/A, resistivity ρ = RA/L, giving SI units of (Ω × m²) / m = Ω·m.

questions.question: What safety device in household circuits melts and breaks the circuit when current exceeds a safe threshold?
questions.explanation: A fuse contains a thin wire with a low melting point that melts by Joule heating when current exceeds the rated limit, opening the circuit.

questions.question: What is the charge of a single electron in Coulombs?
questions.explanation: The elementary charge carried by an electron is approximately -1.602 × 10⁻¹⁹ Coulombs.

questions.question: Which material is traditionally used for the soft core of an electromagnet?
questions.explanation: Soft iron is used because it has high magnetic permeability and low retentivity, magnetizing strongly under current and quickly demagnetizing when current ceases.

questions.question: What is the electrical potential of the Earth conventionally assumed to be?
questions.explanation: Because of its enormous capacitance and volume, adding or removing charge does not alter the Earth's potential, so it is taken as reference zero potential (0 V).

questions.question: Why does a glass rod become positively charged when rubbed with a silk cloth?
options: Electrons transfer from the glass rod to the silk cloth
Protons transfer from the silk cloth to the glass rod
Friction creates brand new positive charges in the glass
The glass rod absorbs neutrons from the air
questions.correct_answer: Electrons transfer from the glass rod to the silk cloth
questions.explanation: Glass has a lower electron affinity than silk. During rubbing, loosely bound electrons migrate from glass to silk, leaving the glass with a net deficit of electrons (positive charge).

questions.question: Why do the leaves of a charged gold-leaf electroscope diverge?
options: Like charges on both leaves repel each other
Unlike charges on the leaves attract each other
Gravitational force pushes the gold leaves upward
Air molecules wedge themselves between the leaves
questions.correct_answer: Like charges on both leaves repel each other
questions.explanation: Both gold leaves acquire the same sign of electric charge from the stem, and mutual electrostatic repulsion forces them apart.

questions.question: What happens to the electrostatic force between two point charges if the distance between them is doubled?
options: The force decreases to one-fourth of its original value
questions.correct_answer: The force decreases to one-fourth of its original value
questions.explanation: By Coulomb's law, F ∝ 1/r². Doubling distance r quadruples r² in the denominator, reducing the force to F/4.

questions.question: Why can electric field lines never intersect each other in space?
options: At an intersection point, the electric field would have two different directions simultaneously, which is impossible
Electric field lines always repel each other like physical wires
Electric field lines can only exist in two dimensions
Intersection would create infinite negative charge
questions.correct_answer: At an intersection point, the electric field would have two different directions simultaneously, which is impossible
questions.explanation: The tangent to an electric field line specifies the unique direction of electric force at that point. If lines crossed, a single point would have two conflicting force vectors.

questions.question: How does conventional current direction relate to the actual flow of conduction electrons in a metal wire?
options: Conventional current flows from positive to negative, while electrons drift from negative to positive
Both flow in the exact same direction from negative to positive
Both flow in the exact same direction from positive to negative
Conventional current flows radially inward while electrons travel circularly
questions.correct_answer: Conventional current flows from positive to negative, while electrons drift from negative to positive
questions.explanation: Historically, current was defined as the flow of positive charge (from high potential + to low potential -). Negatively charged electrons actually drift toward the positive terminal.

questions.question: How does the electrical resistance of a metallic conductor change when its temperature rises?
options: Resistance increases because vibrating lattice ions scatter drifting electrons more frequently
Resistance decreases because heat creates extra electrons
Resistance remains strictly constant regardless of temperature
questions.correct_answer: Resistance increases because vibrating lattice ions scatter drifting electrons more frequently
questions.explanation: Thermal energy increases lattice vibrations in the metal. The increased vibrational amplitude impedes electron drift, shortening relaxation time and increasing resistance.

questions.question: What is the difference between electromotive force (EMF) and potential difference across battery terminals during discharge?
options: EMF is the open-circuit voltage; terminal potential difference is less than EMF due to internal resistance drop (Ir)
EMF is always smaller than terminal voltage
EMF is measured in Newtons, whereas potential difference is measured in Volts
EMF is only present in alternating current circuits
questions.correct_answer: EMF is the open-circuit voltage; terminal potential difference is less than EMF due to internal resistance drop (Ir)
questions.explanation: EMF is the energy per unit charge supplied by the chemical reaction. When current I flows, internal resistance r causes a voltage drop Ir, so terminal voltage V = E - Ir.

questions.question: Why are household electrical appliances connected in parallel rather than in series?
options: Each appliance receives the full supply voltage and can be switched on or off independently
Parallel connection requires less copper wiring throughout the house
Parallel connection eliminates electric current completely
If one appliance fails, all other appliances in parallel turn off automatically
questions.correct_answer: Each appliance receives the full supply voltage and can be switched on or off independently
questions.explanation: In parallel, every branch experiences the same 220 V line voltage and operates independently; switching off one device does not break the circuit for others.

questions.question: Why does a bird perching with both feet on a single uninsulated 11,000 V high-voltage wire not get electrocuted?
options: Both feet rest on the same wire, so the potential difference across its body is virtually zero
Birds have thick rubbery scales that provide infinite electrical insulation
High-voltage alternating current cannot flow through living organisms
The bird is grounded directly to the clouds
questions.correct_answer: Both feet rest on the same wire, so the potential difference across its body is virtually zero
questions.explanation: Current requires a potential difference (V = IR). Because the bird's feet touch points on the wire separated by millimeters, ΔV is negligible and virtually no current flows through the bird.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the third (earth/ground) pin in a standard domestic 3-pin plug?
options: It connects the metal chassis of the appliance safely to the ground to prevent shock during a fault
It delivers additional electric current to boost appliance power
It filters out electrical noise from the utility grid
It acts as a return path for neutral current during normal operation
questions.correct_answer: It connects the metal chassis of the appliance safely to the ground to prevent shock during a fault
questions.explanation: If a live wire touches the metal casing, the low-resistance earth wire carries the fault current safely to the ground, blowing the fuse or tripping the MCB instead of shocking a user.

questions.question: Why does a solenoid behave like a bar magnet when an electric current passes through it?
options: Circular magnetic fields from individual turns add constructively inside the solenoid, creating magnetic poles at its ends
The electric current magnetizes air molecules inside the coil into iron atoms
The copper wire turns into permanent neodymium metal when heated
The battery supplies magnetic fluid directly through the circuit
questions.correct_answer: Circular magnetic fields from individual turns add constructively inside the solenoid, creating magnetic poles at its ends
questions.explanation: Current in adjacent loops produces magnetic field vectors that reinforce each other along the central axis, creating a uniform interior field with distinct North and South poles at opposite ends.

questions.question: What role does Fleming's Left-Hand Rule play in electric motors?
options: It determines the direction of the mechanical force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field
It determines the direction of induced current in a generator
It calculates the resistance of the armature coil
It measures the battery voltage required to rotate the motor
questions.correct_answer: It determines the direction of the mechanical force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field
questions.explanation: Fleming's Left-Hand Rule relates field (Forefinger), Current (Middle finger), and mechanical Force/Motion (Thumb) in motors.

questions.question: Why cannot a transformer be operated with a steady, direct current (DC) power source?
options: A steady DC current produces a static magnetic flux, so no changing flux exists to induce an EMF in the secondary coil
DC current reverses direction too rapidly for the iron core
DC voltages are always too high for transformer copper windings
Transformers only have one coil and cannot conduct DC
questions.correct_answer: A steady DC current produces a static magnetic flux, so no changing flux exists to induce an EMF in the secondary coil
questions.explanation: Faraday's law requires a time-varying magnetic flux (dΦ/dt ≠ 0). A steady DC source creates a constant magnetic field, resulting in zero secondary induced EMF and potentially burning the primary.

questions.question: Why is electrical power transmitted over long cross-country distances at ultra-high voltages?
options: Stepping up voltage reduces current, drastically decreasing I²R Joule heating losses along transmission cables
High voltage pushes electricity faster than the speed of light
Cables can only conduct current when voltage exceeds 100,000 V
High voltage keeps the wires warm to prevent birds from landing
questions.correct_answer: Stepping up voltage reduces current, drastically decreasing I²R Joule heating losses along transmission cables
questions.explanation: For a given transmitted power P = VI, increasing V reduces current I proportionally. Heat dissipation in cables is P_loss = I²R; reducing I by a factor of 10 cuts power loss by 100.

questions.question: Why is the core of a transformer laminated into thin sheets insulated from one another?
options: To minimize energy losses caused by circulating eddy currents
To make the transformer lighter and cheaper to manufacture
To prevent magnetic flux from leaving the primary coil
To insulate the iron core against lightning strikes
questions.correct_answer: To minimize energy losses caused by circulating eddy currents
questions.explanation: Alternating magnetic flux induces eddy currents in the bulk iron core. Lamination into thin varnished sheets breaks up conduction loops, vastly reducing eddy current heating losses.

questions.question: How does Lenz's law reflect the fundamental principle of conservation of energy?
options: The mechanical work done against the opposing induced magnetic force is converted into electrical energy
Lenz's law allows electrical energy to be created from nothing
Induced EMF destroys magnetic fields to create kinetic motion
Conservation of energy applies only to static charges, not magnetic fields
questions.correct_answer: The mechanical work done against the opposing induced magnetic force is converted into electrical energy
questions.explanation: If induced EMF aided the flux change instead of opposing it, a tiny push would trigger runaway magnetic amplification without external work, violating energy conservation.

questions.question: What happens when two identical resistors are connected in parallel compared to their series connection?
options: The equivalent resistance in parallel is one-fourth of the series resistance
The parallel resistance is equal to the series resistance
The parallel resistance is half the series resistance
The parallel resistance is four times the series resistance
questions.correct_answer: The equivalent resistance in parallel is one-fourth of the series resistance
questions.explanation: For two resistors R: in series R_s = 2R; in parallel R_p = R/2. Therefore, R_p / R_s = (R/2) / (2R) = 1/4.

questions.question: Why does a lightning conductor protect tall buildings from lightning strikes?
options: Its sharp metal spikes neutralize storm cloud charge by point discharge and safely ground any direct strike
It reflects lightning flashes back into the upper stratosphere
It turns lightning into household alternating current
It is made of rubber that repels electric charges
questions.correct_answer: Its sharp metal spikes neutralize storm cloud charge by point discharge and safely ground any direct strike
questions.explanation: A lightning rod's pointed spikes leak ions to neutralize induced charges on the roof (corona discharge) and provide a thick copper low-resistance path to direct any strike harmlessly to ground.

questions.question: Why is an ammeter always connected in series in an electrical circuit, whereas a voltmeter is connected in parallel?
options: An ammeter measures current flowing through a branch (low resistance); a voltmeter measures potential difference across components (high resistance)
An ammeter has very high resistance to block current
A voltmeter draws all the current to prevent overloading
Connecting an ammeter in series causes it to act as a battery
questions.correct_answer: An ammeter measures current flowing through a branch (low resistance); a voltmeter measures potential difference across components (high resistance)
questions.explanation: Ammeters have negligible internal resistance so they don't impede the branch current. Voltmeters have enormous resistance so they draw virtually zero current when placed across a component.

questions.question: What happens to the magnetic field strength inside a solenoid if the number of turns per unit length is doubled while current is kept constant?
options: The magnetic field strength is halved
The magnetic field strength remains unchanged
questions.explanation: The magnetic field inside an ideal solenoid is B = μ₀nI. Doubling the turn density n directly doubles the magnetic field strength B.

questions.question: Why does inserting a dielectric material between the plates of an isolated charged capacitor increase its capacitance?
options: The dielectric polarizes, reducing the net electric field and potential difference for a given charge
The dielectric conducts charge between the plates
The dielectric eliminates all electric flux lines
The dielectric generates extra electrons on the positive plate
questions.correct_answer: The dielectric polarizes, reducing the net electric field and potential difference for a given charge
questions.explanation: Dipoles in the dielectric align against the applied field, reducing net E and voltage V between the plates. From C = Q/V, a smaller V for the same charge Q means increased capacitance C = κC₀.

questions.question: How does a galvanometer differ from an ammeter?
options: A galvanometer detects tiny currents and their direction; an ammeter is a modified galvanometer with a low-resistance shunt to measure larger currents
An ammeter cannot detect current direction
A galvanometer has a higher current carrying capacity than an industrial ammeter
questions.correct_answer: A galvanometer detects tiny currents and their direction; an ammeter is a modified galvanometer with a low-resistance shunt to measure larger currents
questions.explanation: A galvanometer is a sensitive pointer instrument that deflects with microamperes. Adding a parallel low-resistance shunt resistor converts it into an ammeter capable of measuring amperes.

questions.question: What is the physical meaning of an electric field at a given point in space?
options: The electrostatic force experienced per unit positive test charge placed at that point (E = F/q)
The total electric charge present in a 1-meter radius
The speed of electrons drifting through that location
The magnetic flux passing through a unit square meter
questions.correct_answer: The electrostatic force experienced per unit positive test charge placed at that point (E = F/q)
questions.explanation: Electric field intensity is defined as force per unit positive test charge: E = F/q. It is a vector pointing in the direction of force on a positive charge.

questions.question: Why does the brightness of a bulb diminish when several identical bulbs are added in series to the same voltage source?
options: Total resistance increases, reducing circuit current and dividing the voltage equally among bulbs
Series connection causes each bulb to draw maximum current from the battery
Each bulb absorbs electric charge permanently
The battery's chemical energy is turned into magnetic field lines
questions.correct_answer: Total resistance increases, reducing circuit current and dividing the voltage equally among bulbs
questions.explanation: In series, R_total = nR, so current drops to I = V/(nR). Power in each bulb is P = I²R = V²/(n²R), which falls off rapidly as n increases, dimming every bulb.

questions.question: Why does an electric heater's connecting cord remain cool while its heating element glows red hot?
options: The heating element has much higher resistance than the copper connecting cord, dissipating nearly all I²Rt heat
The connecting cord is hollow and filled with cooling liquid
Current only flows through the heating element and skips the cord
The connecting cord is made of ceramic insulator
questions.correct_answer: The heating element has much higher resistance than the copper connecting cord, dissipating nearly all I²Rt heat
questions.explanation: By Joule's law H = I²Rt, the same series current flows through both. The nichrome element has much higher resistivity and resistance than copper wire, concentrating heat generation in the element.
